title: Flag Emojis on Windows
summary: Windows does not render flag emoji as images, so flags appear as two-letter country codes in VS Code and pgAdmin. This only matters for the flag quiz project in the browser, where Firefox shows them correctly.

concepts.heading: Key takeaways
points: On Windows, flag emoji show as letter codes in VS Code, pgAdmin and Chrome. Data in .csv files and the database is still correct.
What matters for the project is how flags render in the browser page, not in the editor or pgAdmin.
Workaround for Windows users on the flag quiz: view the app in Firefox, which draws flag emoji.
(Extra) The notes are based on the lesson text as mirrored in the reference repo, since the article could not be read inline.

pitfalls: Assuming the data is broken when you only see country codes instead of flags.
